chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, those who love one another for the sake of Allah on the Day of Resurrection will be upon pulpits of light. The light of their faces, and the light of their bodies, and the light of their pulpits will have illuminated everything, to the extent that they will be recognized by it, so it will be said, "These are the ones who loved one another for the sake of Allah."'

key_terms.الْمُتَحَابِّينَ فِي اللَّهِ: Those who love one another for the sake of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for those who love each other for the sake of Allah on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlighting the spiritual reality of *al-muhibbin fi Allah* (those who love for the sake of Allah) as a distinct eschatological rank. The radiance of their faces, bodies, and pulpits serves as a divine sign (*ayah*) of their purity, distinguishing them from others on the Day of Judgment. This concept underscores the Shia belief that interpersonal relationships grounded in divine love transcend worldly ties and manifest as tangible light in the afterlife.
